name: gap_fade_large_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Large gaps (>1.5%) in NIFTY 50 stocks are disproportionately caused by overnight sentiment over-reaction to global cues (US market moves, Asian open, commodity prices) rather than stock-specific news. When no earnings or corporate action drives the gap, large gaps fade (partially revert) 55-60% of the time because the overnight price impact overshoots the fundamental information content. The key insight is that Indian markets open 4-5 hours after US close, and overnight futures already priced in the US move — the cash market open often over-extends due to retail market orders at open. Fading the excess (the gap beyond what NIFTY futures implied) captures this over-reaction.
stock_filter: gap > 1.5% (absolute); no earnings/corporate action; daily volume > ₹300cr
indicators: excess_gap = gap_pct - NIFTY_implied_gap_pct  # stock gap beyond index gap

conditions: no earnings or corporate action for the stock today
long.confirmation: MACD_line crosses above MACD_signal (momentum turning) AND volume_climax == False (selling exhaustion)

conditions: no earnings or corporate action for the stock today
short.confirmation: MACD_line crosses below MACD_signal AND volume_climax == False

entry.entry_price: market order at MACD signal cross

exit.target: revert 40% of the excess_gap (not full gap, just the excess over index)
exit.stop_loss: gap extends further by 0.5% from open OR 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: once 20% of excess_gap recovered, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 14:00 IST (leave buffer for potential continuation)
exit.signal_exit: if volume_climax fires in gap direction while in trade, exit (new institutional flow confirming gap)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; above 25, large gaps are often structural
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:30 IST; if no setup by 10:30, skip
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not gapping > 2% in same direction (systemic event, don't fade)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.06% at entry (large gaps can widen spreads)
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip if stock has earnings, board meetings, M&A news, regulatory actions, analyst target changes today
other_filters: skip if gap is caused by sector-wide news affecting all peers equally

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — large gap fading is behavioral (retail FOMO at open) and unlikely to be arbitraged away

weaknesses: The news filter is imperfect — sometimes gaps are driven by leaked information, off-market block deals, or global events that fundamentally justify the gap, leading to gap-and-go instead of fade
Low frequency: large gaps (>1.5%) occur on only ~15-20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring monitoring of the full NIFTY 50 universe for sufficient signals
Wider bid-ask spreads at open on gap days increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly eating into the edge vs normal days
prior_art: Dyl & Maberly (1992) gap reversal; Fabozzi et al. (2007) on overnight gap return predictability. Indian context similar to findings in Aggarwal & Gupta (2009) on NSE opening returns.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 80bps - 0.44 * 45bps = 44.8 - 19.8 = 25bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (higher slippage at open). Net ~13bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg, daily edge ~6.5bps. The 35bps estimate includes occasional very large gaps (>3%) where fade profit is 100+ bps. Highly asymmetric return distribution.
